claims.text: Role in hyponatremia: hypervolemic w HF: an ACEi plus a loop diuretic can correct refractory hyponatremia;
claims.quote: In patients with heart failure, an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor, in conjunction with a loop diuretic, can correct refractory hyponatremia.

claims.text: if fluid restriction fails: escalating loop diuretic doses, sometimes w IV 0.9% saline;
claims.quote: In other patients in whom simple fluid restriction is ineffective, a loop diuretic in escalating doses can be used, sometimes in conjunction with IV 0.9% normal saline.

claims.text: replace K and other lytes lost in the urine;
claims.quote: Potassium and other electrolytes lost in the urine must be replaced.

claims.text: SIADH: a loop diuretic may be combined w IV 0.9% saline.
claims.quote: Additionally, a loop diuretic may be combined with IV 0.9% saline as in hypervolemic hyponatremia.

claims.text: Interactions (all diuretics): lithium—⍉, diuretics cut its clearance and risk toxicity;
claims.quote: Lithium generally should not be given with diuretics because they reduce lithium’s renal clearance and add a high risk of lithium toxicity.

claims.text: NSAIDs can blunt the diuretic and antiHTN effect of loop, K-sparing and thiazide diuretics.
claims.quote: the administration of a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory agent can reduce the diuretic, natriuretic, and antihypertensive effects of loop, potassium-sparing and thiazide diuretics

claims.text: OD: supportive—replace fluid and lyte losses;
claims.quote: Treatment of overdosage is supportive and consists of replacement of excessive fluid and electrolyte losses.

claims.text: check lytes, CO2 and BP often.
claims.quote: Serum electrolytes, carbon dioxide level and blood pressure should be determined frequently.
